record.paper_title: Some open problems in computational algebraic geometry
record.original_question: Determine all algebraic curves of genus g <= 10 whose Jacobian is isogenous to a product of elliptic curves.

evidence.quote: Problem 13. Determine all algebraic curves of genus g <= 10 such that their Jacobian splits into a product of elliptic curves.

artifact.self_contained_problem: A smooth projective algebraic curve $C$ of genus $g$ over $\mathbb{C}$ is said to have a completely split Jacobian if its Jacobian variety $\mathrm{Jac}(C)$ is isogenous to a product $E_1 \times E_2 \times \cdots \times E_g$ of elliptic curves. For each integer $g$ with $2 \le g \le 10$, determine (classify) all smooth projective algebraic curves of genus $g$ whose Jacobian is isogenous to a product of $g$ elliptic curves.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is classical and only partially understood. For genus 2, elliptic subcovers were classified going back to Jacobi (degree 2) with extensions through the 19th and 20th centuries; modern computational classifications exist for small degrees. Specific examples are known in higher genera (e.g., Bring's curve in genus 4 has a Jacobian isogenous to a product of four isogenous elliptic curves), and families with isogenous components have been constructed, but a complete classification across all genera up to 10 has not been achieved.

status_evidence.title: Curves of genus 2 with split Jacobian
status_evidence.snippet: Classification of genus 2 curves admitting maps to elliptic curves.
status_evidence.claim: Genus 2 case has been extensively studied with classifications for small subcover degrees.

status_evidence.title: Genus two curves covering elliptic curves: a computational approach
status_evidence.snippet: Jacobi (1832) gives a complete description for n = 2; cases n=3,5 studied later.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial classifications exist, organized by elliptic subcover degree.

status_evidence.title: Families of split Jacobians with isogenous components (Djukanović)
status_evidence.snippet: Constructions of families of curves whose Jacobians split into isogenous elliptic factors.
status_evidence.claim: Active research continues to produce families rather than complete classifications.
